hints.title: Find the tangent gradient
hints.body: Write 2/x2 as a power of x. Differentiate, then substitute x=1.
hints.recap: The derivative gives the tangent gradient.
hints.pitfall: Use the given input, not the height, in the derivative.
hints.pause: Find the point on the curve and its tangent gradient.

recall.reminder: The derivative gives the tangent gradient.

hints.title: Find the normal line
hints.body: The normal is perpendicular to the tangent. If the tangent gradient is m, the normal gradient is −1/m.
hints.recap: Perpendicular nonvertical lines have gradients whose product is −1.
hints.pitfall: Changing only the sign does not give the normal gradient.
hints.pause: Write the normal equation through the point you found.

recall.reminder: Perpendicular nonvertical lines have gradients whose product is −1.

hints.title: Find the two ends of the segment
hints.body: Set y=0 in the line equation for one intercept, then x=0 for the other.
hints.recap: Axis intercepts have one coordinate equal to zero.
hints.pitfall: The segment is sloping; its length is not just the difference of x-coordinates.
hints.pause: Use Pythagoras on the horizontal and vertical distances between the intercepts.

recall.reminder: Use Pythagoras to find a length from the two perpendicular sides of a right triangle.

solution:
dy/dx=−4x−3, so the tangent gradient at x=1 is −4 and the normal gradient is 1/4. The normal through (1,2) is y−2=(x−1)/4.

Putting y=0 gives x=−7; putting x=0 gives y=7/4. The distance between the intercepts is 72+(7/4)2=717/4.

Answer C.
